# Tracked Items Standard

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-25 (initial — supersedes [Documentation Standard § Deferred Work](./documentation_standard.md))

**Status:** RATIFIED. **Contract version `v1`** — see §7.

**Governs** every store of items that persist across sessions and await a decision or an action. Four stores, one location, one shared core, one triage discipline.

---

## §0 Why this is not the thing that was banned

The corpus retired a carried-work ledger on 2026-08-07 after it accumulated **139 items across nine files, eight of which never had a single item triaged out.** [Documentation Standard § Deferred Work](./documentation_standard.md) calls recreating it *"a violation rather than a fallback."*

**That prohibition stands, and this standard does not weaken it.** Four stores could easily be four times the same failure. **Three properties separate a tracked store from a ledger, and every store here MUST have all three:**

1. **An admission test** — a stated rule for what does NOT belong. A store that accepts anything is the banned shape regardless of what it is called.
2. **A triage cadence with a named runner** — someone whose job it is to rule on entries, on a schedule.
3. **An exit.** Every item reaches a terminal state. **An item that survives three consecutive triage passes without a ruling is itself a finding**, reported at the next standup — not carried silently a fourth time.

**A store missing any of the three is out of conformance**, and the correct response is to fix the store or delete it, never to keep filing into it.

---

## §1 The four stores (binding)

All four live at **`development/tracked/<store>/`**, one directory per store, **one file per item.**

| Store | Directory | Holds | Admission test — what does NOT belong |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Issues** | `tracked/issues/` | Deferred work with a clean done-state and a proposed action | Anything achievable in the current PR (fix it), anything with no done-state (that is a tracker item), anything needing evidence before it can be ruled (that is a research candidate) |
| **Tracker** | `tracked/tracker/` | **Operating state and continuity** — live work with no single done-state: a multi-day migration, an incident, a standing condition | Anything with a clean done-state and a proposed action (that is an issue), planned development work (that is a sprint item) |
| **Research candidates** | `tracked/research/` | A question that evidence could settle, awaiting triage into a research cycle | An opinion with no researchable question; a decision already made elsewhere in the corpus |
| **Standards candidates** | `tracked/standards/` | A proposed amendment to a **named** standard, with an anchor precise enough to act on | A general complaint with no target section; an amendment already ratified; a *code* conformance defect (that is an issue) |

**Why file-per-item rather than one table per store.** Several sessions file concurrently. A single file makes every concurrent write a merge conflict on the artifact least able to afford being stale — which is why the tracker previously lived outside the repo entirely. **File-per-item is the platform's existing answer to exactly this** ([Desired State Standard §3](../development/desired-state/desired_state_standard.md): file-per-host, file-per-VM, file-per-service; the all-in-one manifest is forbidden). Two sessions touching different items never conflict; two touching the same item have a real conflict that deserves a human.

**Reading is a rendered view, not the store.** A folder of forty files is unreadable by hand. [`common/dev_ui`](../../development/common/dev_ui/roadmap.md) renders each store as a table **derived from the files**, so the store optimises for safe concurrent writing and the view optimises for reading. **The rendered table is never the source and is never edited.**

---

## §2 Identity (binding)

**`<PREFIX>-<8 random lowercase alphanumerics>`** — e.g. `S-a1b2c3d4`. The filename is `<id>.md`.

| Store | Prefix |
|---|---|
| Issues | `I-` |
| Tracker | `T-` |
| Research candidates | `C-` |
| Standards candidates | `S-` |

**Random, not sequential, and the reason is not collision probability.** Sequential allocation requires **reading the store to learn the next number**, so two sessions filing at once both read the same maximum and both write the same id. **Random makes filing a pure write** — no read, no maximum, no race. At 8 alphanumerics the collision probability is negligible; the race it removes is not hypothetical, and it is why `candidates.md` moved off `C-NNN`.

**The prefix costs two characters and buys context-free identification.** An id in a PR body or a commit message says what kind of thing it is without a lookup.

**Ids are immutable and never reused**, including after an item reaches a terminal state.

---

## §3 The shared core (binding — this is the contract CDF writes against)

Every item file opens with this frontmatter. **Fields below are required in every store**; each store adds its own in §4.

```yaml
---
id: S-a1b2c3d4
title: <one line — the consequence, not the mechanism>
status: <per-store vocabulary, §4>
count: 1
filed: 2026-08-25
filed_by: <PM1 | PM2 | PM3 | operator | <workflow-name>>
---
```

Then a body: what it is, why it matters, and the proposed action. **Every item carries a proposed action** — including one being rejected, where the reasoning *is* the action.

### §3.1 `count` — recurrence is a priority signal, and any filer may increment it

**When an item is surfaced again by a different run or a different session, increment `count` and append a one-line recurrence note.** Do not open a second item.

```
count: 3
```
```markdown
## Recurrences
- 2026-08-19 · review-pr on skyy-command#241
- 2026-08-25 · plan-feature on common/dev_ui
```

**Incrementing is not amending.** The corpus's column-ownership rules forbid editing another filer's reasoning; **a count is not reasoning, and the recurrence note is additive.** This clause exists to retire a documented workaround — the rule that told a run to *"report the recurrence with its count where you are already working, and edit nobody's row"* was routing around a missing integer.

**Recurrence outranks age.** A `count: 3` item filed last week is more real than a `count: 1` filed in June — one is a pattern, the other may be noise. **Triage sorts by count first.**

---

## §4 Per-store extensions and triage (binding)

| Store | Extra fields | Terminal states | Triage cadence · runner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Issues** | `repo:` (where the work lands) | `resolved` · `rejected` | Sprint close-out · the sprint's owner |
| **Tracker** | `state:` (`blocked`/`queued`/`in-progress`/`resolved`) · `ownership:` · `blocked_on:` · `ready:` (**operator-only**) | `resolved`, pruned ≥14 days after | Every standup · whoever runs it |
| **Research candidates** | `component:` · `size:` · `decision:` | `adopted` · `rejected` | `triage-candidates` · PM3 |
| **Standards candidates** | `target:` (the standard) · `anchor:` (section or line) · `ratification:` | `ratified` · `amended` · `rejected` | Standards pass · **PM3 + operator** |

**`ready:` on a tracker item is the operator's alone.** It is an authorisation to act, not a statement about blockedness — an item can be entirely unblocked and still `not-ready` because it is not its turn.

**`ratification:` on a standards candidate is the operator's alone**, per [Standards Governance](../../claude-dot-files/config/rules/standards-governance.md). **Autonomous work MAY file a standards candidate** — Governance explicitly permits surfacing *"gaps, drift, deviations, ADR candidates"* — and MUST NOT edit the standard. **Filing is the permitted surface; this store is its destination.**

### §4.1 Why a standards candidate needs an anchor

Measured 2026-08-25: **21 findable surfaced amendments across at least 8 different heading wordings, 95 further files mentioning amendments in prose no pattern can classify, and exactly ONE of the 21 recording a ratification state.** They were unenumerable, so nothing could triage them and nothing did.

**An amendment with no named target and no anchor cannot be acted on, so it is not admissible.** That is the admission test doing its job.

---

## §5 GitHub Issues are retired (binding)

**No new GitHub issue is filed for tracked work in any MDC repository.** Open issues migrate to `tracked/issues/`; closed issues stay closed in GitHub as history and are not migrated.

**Why:** a repo-tracked store is visible to every developer on every deployment without an API call or an account, it diffs and reviews like everything else, and it renders offline. GitHub's native affordances that are genuinely lost — notification, and the automatic *closed-by-PR* linkage — are replaced by the `repo:` field and by naming the id in the closing commit.

### §5.1 The residue sweep is binding and it is the half that gets forgotten

[Documentation Standard § Retiring a tracking surface](./documentation_standard.md) binds it, and it applies to this retirement in full:

> *"Deleting the artifact does not delete the instruction to rebuild it, and the instruction is the durable part. An actor that reads 'record it in X' and finds no X will create X, correctly believing it is following the rule."*

**Every instruction that says to file a GitHub issue MUST be found and changed** — in this repo's standards and CLAUDE.md files, in agent and skill definitions, and in the workflow prompts that route findings. **A retirement that migrates the items and leaves the instructions is not a retirement**; it is a rename that regrows.

---

## §6 Placement — where an item goes, in order

1. **Resolve it now.** If the fix is small and the context is loaded, do it. Recording an item that takes longer than the fix is the smell.
2. **A phase checkbox**, if it is trigger-gated work on a phase that owns the trigger.
3. **Expand an existing item**, if it is related to one.
4. **A tracked store**, per §1's admission tests.

**Unchanged from the superseded section, and still the point:** these are ordered, and reaching for step 4 first is the failure. What changed is only *where* step 4 lands.

---

## §7 The contract, and why it is versioned

**§2 and §3 are the contract** that tooling in `claude-dot-files` writes against. This document is its owner; consumers conform to it.

**Contract version: `v1`.** Any change to §2 or §3 increments it.

**This exists because the failure already happened.** `candidates.md` changed shape three times in three days and this repo discovered each change as a **failed dispatch** — an unversioned contract between two repos, with no way to tell a schema change from any other pull. **With four stores the failure mode multiplies**, so: a version, and a pre-dispatch check that compares the expected core against what a store actually carries.

---

## §8 Breaking it looks like

- A tracked store with no admission test, no cadence, or no exit — **that is the banned ledger wearing a new name**
- A second surface for any of the four classes: a per-sprint carried-work file, a "loose ends" doc, a holding section in a phase doc
- A new GitHub issue filed for tracked work, or an instruction left in place telling someone to file one
- A sequential id, or an id reused after a terminal state
- A second item opened for something already filed, instead of `count` incremented
- A standards candidate with no named target or no anchor
- An autonomous run **editing** a standard rather than filing a candidate
- An item ruled `ready` or `ratified` by anything other than the operator
- **A rendered table edited directly** — it is derived; the file is the store
- An item carried through three triage passes without a ruling and without that being reported
